steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Quarks (u,d,s,c,b,t) in baryons (3) and mesons (q q̄); Leptons (e,μ,τ,νₑ,ν_μ,ν_τ)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Interactions: strong (gluons, q-q), weak (W+/-, Z⁰, β decay), EM (γ, charged), gravity (negligible)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Conservation: charge, B, L, S in strong/EM; only charge, B-L in weak

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Photoelectric: hf = φ + KE_max; threshold f₀ = φ/h; no time lag; intensity ∝ number of photons

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Electrons accelerated through 150 V. Find de Broglie wavelength and explain if diffraction observable --- Solution: λ = h/sqrt(2meV) = 6.63x10⁻^3⁴ / sqrt(2x9.11x10⁻^3¹x1.6x10⁻¹⁹x150) ≈ 1.0x10⁻¹⁰ m = 0.1 nm. Comparable to atomic spacing -> diffraction observable (e.g. Davisson-Germer)

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Energy of photon with λ = 400 nm | In β⁻ decay: n -> p + e⁻ + ν̄ₑ. Check conservation laws | Find de Broglie λ for electron at 100 eV

steps.title: Lesson plan
steps.body: Starter (5 min): Recall prior knowledge of particles and quantum physics with quick questions. Teaching (15 min): Work through each of the learning objectives, explaining principles step by step. Key points review (5 min): Revisit the key points together, confirming understanding. Worked example (10 min): Model the example question: Electrons accelerated through 150 V. Find de Broglie wavelength and explain if diffraction observable. Solution: λ = h/sqrt(2meV) = 6.63x10⁻^3⁴ / sqrt(2x9.11x10⁻^3¹x1.6x10⁻¹⁹x150) ≈ 1.0x10⁻¹⁰ m = 0.1 nm. Comparable to atomic spacing -> diffraction observable (e.g. Davisson-Germer) Practice (10 min): Students attempt the practice questions independently; circulate and support. Plenary (5 min): Review answers and address misconceptions.
